learn.hook: A noisy cricket fan and a quiet painter — can they be best friends? Let's read and see!
points: 'The Unlikely Best Friends' is about a friendship between two people who seem very different.
'Unlikely' means not expected. An unlikely friendship is one people would not expect.
Good friends can have different hobbies, habits and backgrounds; what matters is respect, trust and care.
Characters change in a story. Notice how their feelings at the start differ from their feelings at the end.
Look for clues in what characters say and do to understand their nature (character traits).

example.q: Read: Tara loved noisy cricket matches. Bholu, her new neighbour, loved quiet painting. "We have nothing in common," Tara grumbled. Then Tara hurt her ankle and had to sit at home for a week. Bholu came over with his paints and taught her to paint the sunset. On Sports Day, when Bholu was nervous before his race, Tara cheered louder than anyone. How did Tara's feelings about Bholu change?
steps: At first Tara said, 'We have nothing in common.'
When she was hurt, Bholu helped her by teaching her to paint.
Later, Tara cheered loudly for Bholu at Sports Day.
So she went from thinking they were too different to being his supportive friend.
example.answer: At first she thought they had nothing in common, but after Bholu helped her, she became his caring friend.

learn.reallife: Your best friend may love maths while you love music — differences can make a friendship more fun.

games.title: Tara and Bholu
items: Tara loved noisy cricket; Bholu loved painting.
The passage calls him her new neighbour.
She had to sit at home for a week.
Bholu taught Tara to play cricket.
He taught her to paint the sunset.
Tara cheered for Bholu on Sports Day.

quiz.q: In the story, Tara loved noisy cricket matches and Bholu loved quiet painting. Why is their friendship 'unlikely'?
quiz.explain: 'Unlikely' means not expected; their very different hobbies make the friendship surprising.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the meaning of 'unlikely'

quiz.q: What did Tara say at first about Bholu?
quiz.explain: Early in the story Tara grumbled, 'We have nothing in common.'
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the beginning and the end of the story

quiz.q: Tara "grumbled" when she said they had nothing in common. 'Grumbled' means she spoke:
quiz.explain: To grumble is to complain in a low, unhappy voice.
quiz.mistake: Guesses the meaning without using the context

quiz.q: When Tara hurt her ankle, what did Bholu do?
options: He taught her to paint the sunset
quiz.explain: Bholu came over with his paints and taught her to paint.
quiz.mistake: Does not find the detail in the passage

quiz.q: Why did Tara cheer louder than anyone on Sports Day?
options: She wanted to win a prize
Bholu was nervous and she wanted to support him
quiz.explain: The passage says Bholu was nervous before his race, so Tara supported him.
quiz.mistake: Ignores the reason given in the passage

quiz.q: Which word best describes Bholu when he visited Tara?
quiz.explain: Visiting a hurt friend and teaching her something new shows that he cares.
quiz.mistake: Does not judge character from actions

quiz.q: What is the main idea of Tara and Bholu's story?
options: Friends can be different and still care for each other
quiz.explain: The story shows two very different children becoming caring friends.
quiz.mistake: Picks a small detail instead of the main idea

quiz.q: Which word is the opposite of 'unlikely'?
quiz.explain: Removing the prefix 'un-' gives 'likely', the opposite.
quiz.mistake: Confuses 'unlikely' with 'unlike'

teach.ask: Gappu wonders: 'I'm a bird and my friend is a squirrel. We're so different. Can we really be best friends?'
teach.praise: Tweet! Different feathers, same kind heart. Squirrel and I will be best friends forever!
teach.nudge: But what really matters in a friendship, if not being the same?

learn.hook: Some of the best stories are tiny true-life moments — just a few lines that show who a person really was.
points: An anecdote is a short, interesting story about a real person or a real event.
Anecdotes are usually told in the past tense and often show a person's character: their wit, kindness or courage.
Many anecdotes are told about Emperor Akbar and Birbal, a witty member of his court. These stories have been told and retold for centuries as popular folk tales.
An anecdote has a setting, a small problem or question, and a clever or surprising ending.
A friendship can be 'unlikely' when two people are very different in age, position or nature, yet value each other.

example.q: Read this anecdote, told in our own words: One day Akbar drew a line on the floor and said, 'Make this line shorter without rubbing out any part of it.' The courtiers were puzzled. Birbal simply drew a longer line beside it. Now Akbar's line looked shorter! What does this anecdote show about Birbal?
steps: The problem: shorten a line without touching it.
Others could not think of a way.
Birbal changed the comparison by drawing a longer line next to it.
example.answer: It shows that Birbal was witty and could think in a clever, unusual way.

learn.reallife: Your grandparents' stories about 'the day the first TV came to our street' are family anecdotes!

games.title: Anecdote or not?
items: a short, funny true story about your grandfather as a boy
a brief story about how a famous scientist solved a puzzle
a little story about what happened at your cousin's wedding

games.title: Line puzzle sequence
items: Akbar drew a line on the floor.
He asked the courtiers to make it shorter without rubbing it out.
Birbal drew a longer line beside it.

quiz.q: What is an anecdote?
options: A short, interesting story about a real person or event
quiz.explain: An anecdote is brief and about something that really happened (or is told as if it did).
quiz.mistake: Confuses an anecdote with any kind of long story

quiz.q: Anecdotes are usually told in which tense?
quiz.explain: They describe something that already happened, so they use the past tense.
quiz.mistake: Does not link storytelling with the past tense

quiz.q: In the anecdote, Akbar asked his courtiers to make his line shorter. What was the tricky condition?
options: They had to use red ink
They could not rub out any part of it
They had to close their eyes
quiz.explain: The challenge was to shorten the line without erasing any part of it.
quiz.mistake: Misses the key condition in the problem

quiz.q: How did Birbal solve the line puzzle?
options: He drew a longer line beside it
He rubbed out half the line
He covered it with a cloth
quiz.explain: Next to a longer line, Akbar's line looked shorter.
quiz.mistake: Thinks he must have erased part of the line

quiz.q: In the anecdote, "The courtiers were puzzled." 'Puzzled' means:
quiz.explain: To be puzzled is to be confused and unable to understand something.
quiz.mistake: Guesses from the word 'puzzle' (a game) without context

quiz.q: Which quality does the line anecdote show in Birbal?
quiz.explain: Wit means quick, clever thinking — exactly what Birbal showed.
quiz.mistake: Does not connect the action with a character trait

quiz.q: Who were Akbar's 'courtiers'?
options: people who attended the emperor at his court
quiz.explain: A court is where a king or emperor met people; courtiers were the people there.
quiz.mistake: Confuses a royal court with a sports court

quiz.q: Why might the friendship of an emperor and a courtier be called 'unlikely'?
options: They were very different in position and power
They spoke to each other only by letters
quiz.explain: An emperor and a member of his court were very different in rank, so a close friendship would be surprising.
quiz.mistake: Does not think about the difference in position

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 'My teacher told an anecdote today. Is that a kind of dinosaur?'
teach.praise: Chirp! An anecdote is a short, true-life story that shows what a person is like. No dinosaurs!
teach.nudge: Is an anecdote made up, or is it about a real person?

learn.hook: Friendship, Birbal, team, palace — all nouns! But each one is a different kind. Let's sort them.
points: A noun names a person, place, animal, thing or idea.
Common nouns are general names (girl, city, river). Proper nouns are particular names and begin with capitals (Tara, Agra, Yamuna).
Collective nouns name a group as one: a team of players, a flock of birds, a herd of cattle, a swarm of bees, a bunch of grapes.
Abstract nouns name feelings, qualities or ideas we cannot see or touch: friendship, kindness, courage, honesty, wisdom.
Many abstract nouns are made with suffixes: friend → friendship, kind → kindness, brave → bravery, wise → wisdom.

example.q: Think it through: Find the kinds of nouns in: 'Birbal's wisdom amazed the crowd in Agra.'
steps: Birbal and Agra are particular names → proper nouns.
Wisdom is an idea we can't touch → abstract noun.
Crowd names a group of people → collective noun.
example.answer: Proper: Birbal, Agra; abstract: wisdom; collective: crowd.

learn.reallife: Your school (proper noun), your class team (collective noun) and your friendship (abstract noun) are all around you!

quiz.q: Which is a proper noun?
quiz.explain: Agra names one particular city, so it is a proper noun.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any place word is a proper noun

quiz.q: Which is an abstract noun?
quiz.explain: Friendship is a feeling or relationship we cannot touch.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up 'friend' (a person) with 'friendship' (an idea)

quiz.q: Fill in the collective noun: a ___ of bees.
quiz.explain: Bees fly in a swarm.
quiz.mistake: Uses the collective noun for a different group

quiz.q: Which is the abstract noun formed from 'brave'?
quiz.explain: Adding -ry gives the noun 'bravery'. 'Bravely' is an adverb.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the adverb with the noun

quiz.q: In 'The team won the match', what kind of noun is 'team'?
quiz.explain: 'Team' names a group of players as one unit.
quiz.mistake: Does not recognise a group word

quiz.q: Which words need capital letters in: 'we visited the taj mahal in agra'?
quiz.explain: Proper nouns (Taj Mahal, Agra) and the first word of a sentence take capitals.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that proper nouns need capitals

quiz.q: What is the abstract noun formed from 'wise'?
quiz.explain: 'Wise' becomes 'wisdom'. 'Wisely' is an adverb and 'wiser' is a comparative.
quiz.mistake: Adds -ness to every adjective

quiz.q: Which is a common noun?
quiz.explain: 'Girl' is a general name; the others are particular names (proper nouns).
quiz.mistake: Confuses common and proper nouns

teach.ask: Gappu chirps: 'I know nouns are naming words. But my teacher says friendship is a noun too. I can't even see it!'
teach.praise: Tweet! Some nouns name things we can see, and abstract nouns name ideas like friendship. I get it!
teach.nudge: Which kind of noun names something we cannot see or touch, like friendship?
